I checked the actual `desloppify` source and your local state. Your model is partially right.

- Auto-injecting stale subjective IDs into the **plan queue** only happens when no non-subjective items remain in `queue_order` ([stale_dimensions.py:169](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:169)).
- But `next` always builds with `include_subjective=True` and below-target threshold, so subjective cards can still appear before full clear ([next.py:212](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/next.py:212), [helpers.py:281](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/helpers.py:281)).
- A stale subjective card is not always “rerun review now.” If open review findings exist for that dimension, the command is `desloppify show review --status open` (real fix/triage work) ([helpers.py:306](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/helpers.py:306)).
- Review rerun is gated by backlog unless you use `--force-review-rerun` ([preflight.py:236](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/preflight.py:236)).

For your current queue: `abstraction_fitness` is stale **and** has `open_review_findings=1`, so next is real work on that review finding first, not just rerun.

And yes, we already reran subjective review today: `abstraction_fitness` has `assessed_at=2026-03-02T14:44:49+00:00` in state. It became stale again after fixes because resolving review findings marks touched dimensions `needs_review_refresh=true` with `refresh_reason=review_finding_fixed` ([resolution.py:40](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_state/resolution.py:40)).

> AGENT

I checked the actual `desloppify` code and your local state, and your intuition is reasonable: the current behavior is a queue-policy mismatch.

Why it happened:
- Resolving review findings marks touched dimensions stale immediately (`needs_review_refresh=true`).
- `next` always includes below-target subjective cards, even with large objective backlog.
- Stale subjective IDs are only auto-injected when no objective plan items remain, but once they’re in `plan.queue_order`, plan ordering can keep them near the top.
- Review reruns are still preflight-gated unless backlog is drained (unless forced), so stale/review prompts can appear before rerun is truly “due.”

I filed the upstream issue with repro + code-path analysis:
- https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify/issues/179

{
  "cmd": "cat > /tmp/desloppify_issue_queue_count_messaging.md <<'EOF'\n## Summary\nQueue reporting is numerically correct but presentation is confusing when plans/clusters are active.\n\nThe headline queue number in `status`/`next` currently reads like a single actionable backlog count, but in practice it mixes levels (leaf findings + synthetic subjective cards - skipped) and does not clearly communicate plan-level workload.\n\n## Concrete example (Mar 2, 2026)\nFrom one workspace:\n- `status`/`next` headline: `Queue: 1934 items remaining`\n- `status`: `open (in-scope): 1942`\n- `status`: `Living plan active: 292 ordered, 23 skipped`\n- `next`: `Subjective: 15 dimensions below target, ...`\n\nThis makes users ask whether 1934 is real debt, clustered tasks, or synthetic queue items.\n\n## Why this is confusing\nA user working the plan expects the headline queue number to represent **plan-level actionable units** (cluster/task queue), not raw leaf finding volume.\n\nCurrent output requires mental reconstruction:\n- 1942 open findings\n- minus 23 skipped\n- plus synthetic subjective queue cards\n- plus cluster/focus behavior\n\nThat is hard to parse quickly during iterative runs.\n\n## Suggestion\nUse a **plan/cluster actionable count as the primary queue number**, with a short bracketed breakdown.\n\nProposed format:\n\n```text\nQueue: 292 plan items [leaf: 1934 | open findings: 1942 | skipped: 23 | subjective cards: 15 | suppressed: 0]\n```\n\nIf a focus cluster is active, include it first:\n\n```text\nQueue: 0 in focus cluster `smart-t1-review` [plan total: 292 | leaf: 1934 | skipped: 23]\n```\n\n## Communication goals\n1. Primary number should map to what the user is expected to work next.\n2. Secondary numbers should explain where the larger counts come from.\n3. Keep it succinct (single line) and stable across `status` and `next`.\n\n## Implementation notes (likely touchpoints)\n- Queue headline rendering:\n  - `desloppify/app/commands/helpers/queue_progress.py`\n- Queue construction/counting behavior:\n  - `desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py`\n  - `plan_aware_queue_count()` uses `build_work_queue(...)`\n- Consider explicit counters for:\n  - plan-actionable items\n  - leaf open findings\n  - skipped\n  - synthetic subjective items\n  - suppressed/ignored\n\n## Related\n- #179 (stale subjective cards surfacing early)\n\nThis issue is about **count semantics and messaging**, so users can trust the queue number at a glance.\nEOF"
}

> AGENT

Yes, this is based on your latest local `documents/desloppify` code (`temp-change`, commit `8dc2d1b`).

Why it happens:
- Queue policy is actually correct for stale-refresh injection: stale subjective dimensions are only appended when no objective items remain in queue ([stale_dimensions.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:169), [stale_dimensions.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:200)).
- But status messaging is not queue-aware: it always prints the stale re-review command whenever stale keys exist ([render.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/status_parts/render.py:301), [render.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/status_parts/render.py:318)).
- It also always prints “Next command to improve subjective scores” when low subjective scores exist, regardless of queue depth ([status_cmd.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/status_cmd.py:161), [subjective.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/helpers/subjective.py:27)).
- Actual reruns are still blocked while objective backlog exists unless forced ([preflight.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/preflight.py:117), [preflight.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/preflight.py:225)).

So this is a UX/message-timing mismatch: the prompt is shown early, even though queue policy/preflight expect queue completion first. If you want, I can patch the status/next rendering so stale-refresh prompts only appear when objective queue is fully drained.

{
  "cmd": "mkdir -p src/shared/runtime && cat > src/shared/runtime/debugRegistry.ts <<'EOF'\ntype ManagedDebugGlobalKey =\n  | '__supabase_client__'\n  | 'supabase'\n  | '__RECONNECT_SCHEDULER__'\n  | '__DATA_FRESHNESS_MANAGER__';\n\ninterface ActiveRegistration {\n  owner: string;\n  value: unknown;\n}\n\nconst activeRegistrations = new Map<ManagedDebugGlobalKey, ActiveRegistration>();\n\nfunction hasWindow(): boolean {\n  return typeof window !== 'undefined';\n}\n\nexport function registerDebugGlobal<K extends ManagedDebugGlobalKey>(\n  key: K,\n  value: NonNullable<Window[K]>,\n  owner: string,\n): () => void {\n  if (!hasWindow()) {\n    return () => {};\n  }\n\n  const globalWindow = window as Window;\n  const hadPrevious = Object.prototype.hasOwnProperty.call(globalWindow, key);\n  const previousValue = globalWindow[key];\n\n  globalWindow[key] = value;\n  activeRegistrations.set(key, { owner, value });\n\n  let disposed = false;\n  return () => {\n    if (disposed || !hasWindow()) {\n      return;\n    }\n    disposed = true;\n\n    const currentRegistration = activeRegistrations.get(key);\n    if (!currentRegistration || currentRegistration.value !== value) {\n      return;\n    }\n\n    if (hadPrevious) {\n      globalWindow[key] = previousValue;\n    } else {\n      delete (globalWindow as Partial<Record<ManagedDebugGlobalKey, unknown>>)[key];\n    }\n\n    activeRegistrations.delete(key);\n  };\n}\n\nexport function getDebugGlobal<K extends ManagedDebugGlobalKey>(key: K): Window[K] | undefined {\n  if (!hasWindow()) {\n    return undefined;\n  }\n  return (window as Window)[key];\n}\n\nexport function getDebugGlobalOwner([REDACTED]): string | null {\n  return activeRegistrations.get(key)?.owner ?? null;\n}\nEOF",

> AGENT

Yes. I traced it in `documents/desloppify`, and your expectation is reasonable. Current behavior is a mix of policy mismatch + one real logic bug.

**What’s happening now**
1. `next` always asks queue builder to include subjective items (`include_subjective=True`), even when objective backlog exists.  
[next.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/next.py:205), [core.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py:85)

2. Subjective items are intentionally built “alongside mechanical” (explicitly tested as no backlog gating).  
[work_queue_cases.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/tests/review/work_queue_cases.py:536)

3. For stale subjective items, generated commands include `--force-review-rerun`, which bypasses rerun backlog guards.  
[helpers.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/helpers.py:418), [preflight.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/app/commands/review/preflight.py:217), [auto_cluster.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py:429)

4. The stale-sync logic that injects `subjective::*` into plan checks only `plan["queue_order"]`, not actual open objective findings in state. So if plan queue is temporarily empty, stale items get injected early.  
[stale_dimensions.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:273)

I confirmed this with a minimal repro: even with an open objective finding in state, empty `queue_order` caused stale injection (`subjective::design_coherence`).

**Why this felt wrong in your run**
- You were in “execute queue” mode, but stale subjective tasks can still surface early by design.
- Suggested commands were forceful, so they bypassed safeguards.
- There’s also a focus leak: if active cluster resolves to empty/missing members, filtering is skipped and unrelated items still show.  
[plan_order.py](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/plan_order.py:114)

**Bottom line**
- This is not just you “using it wrong.”  
- Current implementation does not enforce “subjective stale refresh only after objective queue is fully drained.”

If you want, I can now patch this in `desloppify` (gating stale subjective surfacing to objective-backlog=0, remove forced rerun from auto-suggested stale actions, and fix empty-focus filtering) and then run the relevant tests.

  "cmd": "cat > /tmp/desloppify_issue_subjective_queue_strict_lifecycle.md <<'EOF'\n## Summary\n`next` can surface **stale subjective re-review work too early** (while objective backlog still exists), and the lifecycle around **strict score refresh** at queue completion is confusing.\n\nThis caused repeated premature subjective reruns in a live run, while strict remained frozen and objective queue work was still pending.\n\n## What I expected\nWhen running the normal execution loop (`next -> fix -> plan done`) with a living plan:\n\n1. Stale subjective reruns should only become actionable when objective queue is truly drained.\n2. At queue-empty transition, we should enter an explicit “review/refresh” phase.\n3. After subjective rerun finishes, strict should be clearly updated/revealed (or auto-refreshed) before returning to triage/planning.\n\n## What happened\n1. `next` includes subjective items alongside objective items by default.\n2. Stale subjective items suggest `review --prepare ... --force-review-rerun`, which bypasses rerun preflight/backlog guards.\n3. Stale injection logic can use `plan.queue_order` emptiness instead of true objective backlog, so stale subjective IDs can appear early.\n4. Strict score stays “frozen at plan start” and the phase transition to refreshed/live strict is not explicit enough at queue-empty + post-rerun checkpoints.\n\n## Relevant code paths\n- Subjective always included in `next` queue build:\n  - `desloppify/app/commands/next.py` (`include_subjective=True`)\n  - `desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py`\n- Stale subjective action suggests forced rerun:\n  - `desloppify/engine/_work_queue/helpers.py` (`primary_command` adds `--force-review-rerun`)\n  - `desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py` (`auto/stale-review` action adds `--force-review-rerun`)\n- Preflight gate bypassed when force flag is present:\n  - `desloppify/app/commands/review/preflight.py`\n- Stale injection based on plan queue content:\n  - `desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py` (`has_real_items` checks `queue_order` only)\n- Current tests explicitly enforce “subjective appears alongside mechanical” behavior:\n  - `desloppify/tests/review/work_queue_cases.py::test_subjective_items_always_appear_alongside_mechanical`\n\n## Proposed fixes\n### A) Actionability gating for stale subjective reruns\n- Only surface **stale** subjective rerun queue items when objective backlog is zero.\n- Keep unassessed/initial subjective handling as-is (or separately configurable).\n\n### B) Remove force from default stale actions\n- Do not auto-suggest `--force-review-rerun` in:\n  - per-item stale subjective `primary_command`\n  - `auto/stale-review` cluster action\n- Let preflight enforce drain-first behavior unless user explicitly chooses force.\n\n### C) Backlog source of truth\n- In `sync_stale_dimensions`, gate injection on actual open objective findings (state/work-queue), not just `plan.queue_order` shape.\n\n### D) Strict score lifecycle UX (queue-empty checkpoints)\nPlease add explicit strict-score updates at both points:\n\n1. **Checkpoint 1: objective queue becomes empty**\n   - Show clear phase banner: objective done -> subjective refresh phase.\n   - Show current strict snapshot and exact next command.\n\n2. **Checkpoint 2: subjective rerun/import completes**\n   - Ensure strict is refreshed/revealed immediately (preferably via automatic scan path).\n   - If strict is still frozen, print a blocking explicit command and reason.\n\n## Acceptance criteria\n- With objective backlog > 0, `next` does not present stale subjective rerun as actionable top work.\n- Default stale subjective commands do not include `--force-review-rerun`.\n- Stale injection does not occur solely because `plan.queue_order` is empty while objective findings still exist.\n- At queue-empty and post-rerun checkpoints, strict score state transition is explicit and visible.\nEOF\n\ngh issue create -R peteromallet/desloppify \\\n  --title \"Stale subjective reruns surface before objective drain; strict-score refresh lifecycle unclear\" \\\n  --body-file /tmp/desloppify_issue_subjective_queue_strict_lifecycle.md"

You’re right to question it. I checked both the code and our current plan/state, and the behavior is misleading.

- `sync_stale_dimensions()` only injects stale subjective IDs when **no objective findings are open**: [stale_dimensions.py:248](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/stale_dimensions.py:248)

2. Why you still see “Re-review … stale” early  
- Auto-clustering builds `auto/stale-review` from **all** `subjective::*` IDs in `plan.queue_order` except unscored, not from actual stale flags: [auto_cluster.py:420](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py:420)  
- Plan ordering always puts `queue_order` items first: [plan_order.py:23](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/plan_order.py:23)

3. What’s true in our current state  
- Actual stale dimensions now: `0`  
- `auto/stale-review` cluster members: `14`  
- Open objective unsuppressed findings: `931`  
So the “stale” label is inaccurate for this state; these are under-target subjective items being treated/labeled as stale by cluster logic.

4. Extra nuance  
- Queue builder hides only subjective items explicitly flagged `stale_review` when objective backlog exists: [core.py:86](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/core.py:86)  
- Non-stale under-target subjective items can still appear if they’re in plan order.

So yes: your expectation (“don’t surface stale re-review until objective queue is done”) is directionally correct, and the current stale cluster labeling/order logic is what’s causing the confusion.

> AGENT

Root cause found. You’re seeing this because of a logic mismatch, not just operator error.

1. Under-target subjective IDs can “stick” in plan queue  
- In [auto_cluster.py:468](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py:468), under-target subjective IDs are appended when objective backlog is empty.  
- But when objective findings return, those IDs are not removed just because objective work exists.

2. Those stuck IDs are mislabeled as stale  
- In [auto_cluster.py:420](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py:420), `auto/stale-review` is built from queue `subjective::*` IDs (minus unscored), not from actual stale state.  
- So non-stale under-target IDs get shown as “Re-review stale subjective dimensions.”

3. Plan order then puts them ahead  
- [plan_order.py:23](/Users/user_c042661f/Documents/desloppify/desloppify/engine/_work_queue/plan_order.py:23) respects `queue_order` first, so these synthetic subjective IDs can rise to the top.

Concrete evidence from current state:
- actual stale dimensions: `0`
- open objective unsuppressed findings: `931`
- `auto/stale-review` cluster still showing `14`

I filed the GitHub issue with full repro + fix proposal:  
- https://github.com/peteromallet/desloppify/issues/186

Proposed fix in the issue:
1. Build stale cluster from actual stale IDs only.  
2. Defer/prune under-target subjective queue IDs whenever objective backlog is non-empty.  
3. Add regression tests for “objective returns after subjective phase” so this can’t recur.

If objective findings reappear after an earlier subjective phase, subjective queue items injected for under-target review should not remain ahead of objective work.\n\n## Actual\n- Under-target subjective IDs can remain in `plan.queue_order` after objective findings come back.\n- Auto-cluster logic classifies all non-unscored `subjective::*` IDs in queue as \"stale\".\n- Result: queue head can show `auto/stale-review` while objective backlog is large.\n\n## Root cause\n### 1) Under-target queue IDs are injected when objective backlog is empty, but not removed when objective backlog returns\nIn `engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py`:\n- under-target IDs are appended to `plan.queue_order` only when `not has_objective_items`.\n- pruning only removes IDs that are no longer under-target (improved score), not IDs that should be deferred because objective work has returned.\n\nSo those IDs persist across later scans even when objective findings are open.\n\n### 2) Stale cluster membership is derived from queue presence, not stale state\nIn `engine/_plan/auto_cluster.py`:\n- `stale_queue_ids` is computed as all subjective queue IDs except unscored.\n- this does not intersect actual stale set from `_current_stale_ids(state)`.\n\nTherefore under-target subjective IDs in queue are mislabeled as stale.\n\n## Proposed fix\n1. **Correct stale cluster membership**\n   -
